function: DenseNet DeepReceiver replacing the full MIMO-OFDM receiver chain: recovers the transmitted bit stream from the received I/Q signal, i.e. signal detection (p. 2).
system: MIMO-OFDM, Nt transmit and Nr receive antennas (values not stated), 64 subcarriers, 64QAM, CP of 1/4 data length; no RIS; band not stated (pp. 1, 4).
method: DenseNet DeepReceiver with global average pooling and n parallel binary classifiers; supervised pretraining on source domain, then fine-tuning last three layers (transfer learning) on target data (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa channels, 3GPP 37.885 Urban scenario; source domain 100,000 training samples, each target domain 10,000 samples for retraining; user moves around a building for 100 s (p. 4).
test_conditions: Pretrained on 100,000 source samples; scene changes at 25 s, fine-tuning starts at 40 s with 10,000 target samples; BER over SNR 0-25 dB (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: ML and MMSE detection with imperfect CSI from channel estimation. Learned: DNN [2] and LSTM [3] receivers, DeepReceiver without retraining (pp. 4-5).
metrics: BER versus SNR; BER over time under channel change; pilot cost; epochs to convergence; loss versus epoch; average BER reduction 10.3% versus ML (pp. 4-5).
complexity: none; only training epochs to convergence (Table II) and pilot counts (Table I) are reported (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "channel model using QuaDRiGa in the 3GPP 37.885 Urban" scenario; source and target data are both generated with it.
q2_support: p. 4: "each target domain employs 10,000 samples" for retraining, against 100,000 in the source domain; "the user changes direction to another side of the building at" 25 s and fine-tuning follows.
q3_support: p. 4: "Classic receivers using maximum likelihood (ML)" and MMSE (non-learned), and "LSTM [3] for signal detection" with DNN [2] (earlier learned receivers); Fig. 4 compares BER.
q4_support: p. 5: "we further assessed the convergence rate of the receivers mentioned" (Table II, epochs); p. 3 only claims qualitatively that binary classifiers cut runtime; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or measured runtime, and the pilots of Table I are signaling overhead.
q5_support: p. 4: "Simulation experiments are conducted using" a GPU; the channels come from the authors' own QuaDRiGa runs, with no link or DOI for code or data, no public dataset and no measured data.
notes: The first page holds the title and DOI. Included as area 1: the DeepReceiver replaces the whole MIMO-OFDM receiver and outputs the bit stream, judged by BER. q1 counts through QuaDRiGa; the scenario is named 3GPP 37.885 Urban (V2X study, another 3GPP document), so the reviewer should confirm. q4 is borderline and marked 0: the paper gives only epochs to convergence (Table II), pilots (Table I) and a 5-second fine-tuning inside the simulated timeline (p. 4), none an order, operations, parameters or measured runtime; it would become 1 only if the reviewer accepts epochs or the 5-second fine-tuning time as the reported cost. Nt, Nr and the carrier frequency are not stated.
